title: Switching from clarinet to saxophone
summary: As clarinets faded he took up alto, learning fingering from Earl Pearson and from George Gino.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: I got back to New Orleans and that's where I met George Gino. He was living about a block from me. He used to pass and he had me practicing on my clarinet. And he stopped there a couple of times and he went home and got his banjo. Him and I on the clarinet. And the clarinet began to die out. Everybody was getting saxophones. Everybody wanted a saxophone player. No clarinets. So I eventually got there a saxophone. And then George used to come by there and we used to sit down and figure out them chords and gather notes and notes. And then they had a fellow by the name of Earl. Now I can't think of his last name but he was playing with Celestan at the time. That's what did he play? He played Alton Sack. He was a Pullman poet on the train. What old would that be?
Pearson or something like that, huh?

Earl Pearson, that's his name. Yeah. Bright, bright fella. Yeah. And he showed me the finger on the saxophone. Alto saxophone? Yeah. And I started playing the saxophone. Then I had a saxophone three weeks on. I played my first job. Oakland
